html:
Laas Geel is a group of rock shelters near Hargeisa in Somaliland whose walls are covered with paintings of cattle, people and dogs, thought to be at least five thousand years old.

The paintings show cows with decorated necks and udders and people with raised arms, often read as cattle worship by early herders. Local people knew the caves, but they became known to science only in 2002, when a French team recorded them.

The bright colours are unusually well kept. They show that cattle herding reached the Horn of Africa thousands of years ago, as in the spread of herding across East Africa, long before the incense trade or the coming of Islam. Laas Geel is now a point of pride for Somaliland.
sum: Laas Geel is a group of rock shelters near Hargeisa in Somaliland whose walls are covered with paintings of cattle, people and dogs, thought to be at least five thousand years old.
